# Appeal of Denial — Cervical Fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551

**Policy relied upon by the plan:** Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02 — https://www.bcbsnd.com/providers/policies-precertification/legacy-medical-policy/c/cervical-fusions (effective 2024-07-01)

**Member:** Rowan Delgado
**Member ID:** W865123628
**Plan:** Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota (Commercial/ACA), North Dakota
**Denial date:** 2026-08-18
**Reference number:** POC-9391F374E1-41425
**Appeal deadline:** Must be received by 2027-02-14

---

To Whom It May Concern:

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my cervical fusion surgery (ACDF, CPT 22551), which was denied as not medically necessary in the notice dated 2026-08-18 (reference number POC-9391F374E1-41425). My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for my condition, and I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision.

I understand the denial was based on the plan's own medical policy, Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02. When I compare that policy's criteria to my medical records, I believe my records show that I meet the plan's own requirements.

### 1. General criteria for ACDF

The policy states:

> "ACDF) is considered medically necessary for treatment of symptomatic degenerative disease when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

### 2. Unremitting radiculopathy refractory to conservative management, with imaging findings

The policy states:

> "unremitting cervical radiculopathy and/or myelopathy (i.e., neck and arm pain) resulting in disability and/or neurological deficit that are refractory to at least six weeks of standard conservative, nonoperative management (e.g., reduced activities, exercise, analgesics, physical therapy), in the absence of progressive or severe myelopathy complex imaging studies (i.e., CT, MRI, X-ray) demonstrate at least ONE of the following at each impacted level being considered for the fusion:"

My records show:

- I have had 14 months of progressive neck pain, with radicular pain and numbness radiating into my right thumb and index finger, along with weakness — this is a neurological deficit, not just pain.
- I completed 8 weeks (18 visits) of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, from 2026-05-18 to 2026-07-13, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This is well beyond the six weeks of conservative management referenced in the policy.
- I also tried NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- My records do not document progressive or severe myelopathy.

### 3. Herniated nucleus pulposus / foraminal stenosis at the level considered for fusion, correlating with exam findings

The policy states:

> " Herniated nucleus pulposus  Spondylosis (i.e., presence of osteophytes)  Visible loss of disc height compared to adjacent levels with resultant foraminal stenosis physical examination findings and imaging studies correlate with each level being considered for the fusion"

My records show:

- MRI of the cervical spine on 2026-06-26 documents a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. This is a herniated nucleus pulposus with resulting foraminal stenosis at the level being considered for fusion.
- On physical examination, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level (C5-C6/C6 nerve root). This is the correlation between physical exam findings and imaging that the policy describes.

### Summary

Based on the plan's own policy language quoted above, and the clinical findings in my records — 14 months of radiculopathy with neurological deficit, more than six weeks of documented conservative treatment (physical therapy, NSAIDs, and injection) without lasting relief, MRI evidence of a herniated disc with foraminal stenosis at C5-C6, and physical exam findings that correlate with that level — I believe the record supports that the plan's own criteria for ACDF have been addressed. I am asking that this determination be reconsidered in light of these records.

### What I am requesting

1. That the plan reconsider and overturn the denial for CPT 22551 (ACDF).
2. That the plan review the full prior authorization packet, including the physical therapy discharge note, imaging report dated 2026-06-26, and my surgeon's clinical documentation.
3. Written confirmation of the outcome of this appeal, sent to me at the address on file.

Please let me know if any additional records are needed from my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, or from my physical therapy provider. I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-14, and I am submitting this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter [insert appeal address from denial letter], or as directed by the number on the back of my insurance card.

Thank you for reconsidering this decision.

Sincerely,

[Rowan Delgado]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Date signed]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
